mainTopic: Who counts as a זקנה, how long an עונה is, when women get דיה שעתה after long breaks, relying on רבי אליעזר in a time of pressure, and the rules for young girls who see blood.
overview: The גמרא finishes defining a זקנה as a woman who is called 'אמא, אמא' without being bothered. It shows how two slightly different wordings of this sign differ in practice. It explains that an average עונה is 30 days if you count the days of טומאה, or 20 days if you count only the days of טהרה. A ברייתא teaches that an older woman who sees blood after three עונות gets דיה שעתה. After this happens three times, she is like all women. The גמרא questions the ברייתא's wording about even and uneven gaps and gives two answers, one following the רבנן and one following רבי דוסא. Next, רבי אליעזר brings a real case to show that any woman who stopped for three עונות gets דיה שעתה. The חכמים reject it as a ruling made under pressure, and the גמרא explains that רבי relied on רבי אליעזר only in a time of pressure, because many sages disagreed with him. The amud ends with a ברייתא about young girls who see blood, and the גמרא begins to examine its last line.

steps.title: Defining an older woman
steps.stepSummary: A זקנה is a woman whom people call 'אמא, אמא' and she is not embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: An older woman is any woman whom people call 'Mother, Mother' and she is not embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical sign for which woman counts as a זקנה (an older woman) for the הלכות of this פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of naming an exact age, the definition uses a social sign. If people naturally call her 'Mother' and she is fine with it, she is considered old.

keyTerms.meaning: An older woman (here, one past childbearing years)

phrases.english: Any woman whom people call
'Mother, Mother,' and she is not embarrassed.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זקנה is a woman called 'אמא אמא' who is not embarrassed by it.

steps.title: Two versions of the definition
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא and רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק disagree. One says the sign is that she does not take offense; the other says it is that she is not embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא and רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק: one says it is any woman who does not take offense, and the other says it is any woman who is not embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give slightly different wordings of the sign for a זקנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One version focuses on whether she minds or objects (מקפדת). The other focuses on whether she feels embarrassed (בושה). At this point we do not yet know whether this changes anything in practice.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא וְרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק —
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira and Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak:
One says: any woman who does not take offense,
and the other says: any woman who is not embarrassed.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינָהּ מַקְפֶּדֶת, וְחַד אָמַר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינָהּ בּוֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the definition in step 1 was worded in two different ways.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One sage defines a זקנה by 'not offended,' the other by 'not embarrassed.'

steps.title: What is the practical difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two wordings.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two wordings lead to different results. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two wordings sound almost the same. The גמרא wants a real case where one version would call her a זקנה and the other would not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two definitions give different results.

steps.title: Embarrassed but not offended
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a woman who feels embarrassed but does not take offense.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a woman who is embarrassed but does not take offense.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two versions differ when a woman blushes at being called 'Mother' but does not object to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the 'not offended' version, she counts as a זקנה, since she does not mind. By the 'not embarrassed' version, she does not count, since she still feels embarrassed.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: A woman called 'Mother' who is embarrassed but does not object is a זקנה according to one sage and not according to the other.

phrases.english: The difference between them is:
she is embarrassed but does not take offense.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case of a woman who is embarrassed but does not take offense.

steps.title: How long is a cycle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long an עונה (a typical cycle) is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how long is an עונה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how many days make up one עונה. The משנה measures a זקנה by 'three עונות,' so we need this number. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about a זקנה depends on three עונות passing without her seeing blood. Without knowing the length of one עונה, we cannot measure that time.

phrases.english: And how long is an עונה?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The number of days in a standard עונה.

steps.title: An average cycle is thirty days
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting רבי יהודה נשיאה, says an average עונה is 30 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה: an average עונה is thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: an average cycle is 30 days long.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the basic measure. By this count, three עונות would be about 90 days.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia:
An average עונה is thirty days,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה

steps.title: רב חסדא says twenty days
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב חסדא, who says an עונה is 20 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said in the name of רב חסדא: twenty days.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer seems to disagree: an עונה is only 20 days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This looks like a clear argument, 30 days against 20 days. The next step explains how both can be right.

phrases.english: And Rava said in the name of Rav Chisda:
Twenty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different number from step 6.

steps.title: They do not really disagree
steps.stepSummary: The two opinions match: one counts both the impure and pure days, and the other counts only the pure days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree. One sage counts the days of impurity and the days of purity, and the other sage does not count the days of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that 30 days and 20 days are really the same cycle, just counted in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה נשיאה counts the whole cycle, both the days of טומאה and the days of טהרה, which comes to 30. רב חסדא leaves out the days of טומאה and counts only the days of טהרה, which comes to 20. So the ten-day difference is simply the days of טומאה.
steps.whatToRemember: An average עונה is 30 days including the days of טומאה, or 20 days counting only the days of טהרה. It is the same length, counted differently.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these two sages argue about how long a woman's cycle is. They agree on the cycle and differ only in which days they include in the count.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree.

phrases.aramaic: מָר קָחָשֵׁיב יְמֵי טוּמְאָה וִימֵי טׇהֳרָה,
phrases.english: One sage counts the days of impurity and the days of purity,
and the other sage does not count the days of impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the seeming argument between steps 6 and 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: the two opinions count different parts of the same cycle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought they argue over whether a cycle is 30 or 20 days.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree. 30 includes the days of טומאה, and 20 leaves them out.

steps.title: An older woman who sees after long breaks
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a זקנה sees blood after three עונות, she is impure only from that moment (דיה שעתה). The same is true the second time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: an older woman for whom three עונות passed, and then she saw blood, her time is enough. If another three עונות passed and she saw blood, her time is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא teaches that an older woman who sees blood after a long break becomes impure only from the moment she sees it. This holds for the first time and the second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a woman who sees blood is considered impure retroactively, for some time before she noticed it. A זקנה who has stopped seeing for three עונות does not get this backward impurity, because seeing blood is not normal for her anymore.

keyTerms.meaning: Her time is enough: she is impure only from the moment she sees, not before

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: an older woman
for whom three עונות passed, and then she saw blood,
her time is enough.
phrases.notes: This means she is impure only from the moment she saw, not going back in time.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד עָבְרוּ עָלֶיהָ שָׁלֹשׁ עוֹנוֹת, וְרָאֲתָה —
phrases.english: And if another three עונות passed and she saw blood,
her time is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: זְקֵנָה שֶׁעָבְרוּ עָלֶיהָ שָׁלֹשׁ עוֹנוֹת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first and second times a זקנה sees blood after three עונות, she is impure only from that moment.

steps.title: After the third time she is like all women
steps.stepSummary: If it happens a third time, she loses the leniency and becomes impure retroactively, like any other woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if another three עונות passed and she saw blood, she is like all women, and she makes things impure for the previous twenty-four hours and back to her last examination.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא teaches that after a third time, the older woman is treated like every other woman and her impurity reaches back in time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing blood three times shows she now has a pattern, so we no longer treat her as someone who has stopped seeing. Her impurity goes back a full twenty-four hours (מעת לעת), or back to her last check (מפקידה לפקידה), like a regular woman.

keyTerms.meaning: From one examination back to the previous examination

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the leniency of דיה שעתה lasts only until a pattern of seeing is set by three sightings.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד עָבְרוּ עָלֶיהָ שָׁלֹשׁ עוֹנוֹת, וְרָאֲתָה —
phrases.english: And if another three עונות passed and she saw blood,
she is like all women,
and she makes things impure for the previous twenty-four hours
and back to her last examination.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the third time, a זקנה becomes impure retroactively, מעת לעת and מפקידה לפקידה.

steps.title: Even uneven gaps count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the rule applies even if the gaps between sightings were shorter or longer than exactly three עונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is not only when the gaps were exactly even. Even if she saw sooner, and even if she saw later.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by saying the three sightings make her like all women even if the breaks between them were not exactly equal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Equal gaps clearly show a pattern, so that case does not need to be taught. The חידוש is that even uneven gaps, shorter or longer, still bring her back to the status of all women after three sightings.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא says the rule holds 'not only with even gaps, but even with shorter or longer gaps.' Step 12 challenges this wording, and steps 14 and 15 give two ways to read it.

phrases.english: And it is not only when the gaps matched exactly,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. Either way, the meaning is 'not only.'

phrases.english: but even if she saw sooner,
and even if she saw later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the rule of step 10 to cover uneven gaps.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Three sightings make a זקנה like all women even when the gaps between them were shorter or longer than exact.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three sightings after long breaks make a זקנה like all women, not only when the gaps were even, but even when they were shorter or longer.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא treat evenly spaced sightings as the obvious case?
steps.stepSummary: The word "אפילו" makes it sound obvious that a זקנה who saw blood at even intervals goes back to being impure retroactively. But even intervals should set up a וסת, so דיה שעתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says "even if she decreased", which suggests that the even-interval case goes without saying. But it is the other way around! If her intervals were even, she has set up a fixed cycle, and she is impure only from that moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording "even if she decreased" in the ברייתא from step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Even" means the ברייתא thinks the even-interval case is the simple one, where she surely becomes retroactively impure. But a woman who sees blood at even intervals has a fixed וסת. According to רבי דוסא, a woman with a וסת is only impure from the moment she sees (דיה שעתה), so the even case should be the more lenient one.

keyTerms.meaning: she decreased: the gap between sightings was shorter
she was even: the sightings came at exactly the same intervals
she has set up her fixed cycle
her time is enough: impure only from the moment she sees, not before

steps.confusionAlert: Here כִּוְּונָה does not mean "intention." It means the sightings came at evenly matched, regular intervals.

phrases.english: "Even if she decreased": so it goes without saying when she was even?
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא from step 11, which said the rule applies even if the gaps were shorter or longer.

phrases.english: On the contrary, when she was even,
she has set up her fixed cycle, and her time is enough!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא's last clause from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word "אפילו" in the ברייתא's last clause.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "Even" treats the even-interval case as the simpler one. But even intervals set up a וסת, and under רבי דוסא that makes her more lenient (דיה שעתה), not stricter.

steps.title: Even under the רבנן, the wording should be reversed
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say the ברייתא follows the רבנן, who hold that even a woman with a וסת is impure מעת לעת. But then the ברייתא should have said "not only uneven, but even even."
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say the ברייתא follows the רבנן, who argue with רבי דוסא and say that a woman with a fixed cycle is impure for the past twenty-four hours. If so, it should have been worded the other way around: "Not only when she decreased or increased, but even when she was even!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible answer to its own question and so makes the challenge stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the רבנן, a וסת does not protect her from retroactive impurity. So the surprising case would be the even one, where you might have thought her fixed cycle helps her. A "not only... but even" sentence should end with the surprising case, so the ברייתא's order still does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say: introduces a possible answer that is about to be rejected
for the past twenty-four hours: impure retroactively for one full day
it should have said the opposite
she increased: the gap between sightings was longer

phrases.english: And if you would say: it follows the רבנן,
who disagree with רבי דוסא,
who say: a woman who has a fixed cycle
makes things impure for the past twenty-four hours,
then it should have said the opposite,
and let it say: and not only when she decreased or increased,
but even when she was even!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off a possible escape from the challenge in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the cases in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the רבנן, the even case is the bigger surprise, so it should come after "even." The ברייתא has the order backwards.

steps.title: First answer: change the wording to match the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Teach the ברייתא this way: "not only when she decreased or increased, but even when she was even."
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it like this: not only when she decreased or increased, but even when she was even.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the ברייתא's wording so the order makes sense under the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this wording, the ברייתא follows the רבנן. A זקנה who goes back to seeing blood is impure retroactively in every case, even when her sightings were evenly spaced.

keyTerms.meaning: not only... but even: a sentence pattern that builds up to the bigger surprise

phrases.english: Teach it this way: not only when she decreased or increased,
but even when she was even.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in steps 12 and 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's "even" treated the even case as obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: With the order reversed, the ברייתא follows the רבנן: she is retroactively impure even with evenly spaced sightings.

steps.title: Second answer: the ברייתא excludes the even case and follows רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: Or read it like this: the rule applies only when she decreased or increased, not when she was even. Even sightings set up a וסת and דיה שעתה. This follows רבי דוסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say this is what it means: not when she was even, only when she decreased or increased. But if she was even, she has set up a fixed cycle, and her time is enough. And whose view is this? It is רבי דוסא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. It keeps the ברייתא as a רבי דוסא teaching and reads it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here "even if she decreased" is not read as including the even case. It is read as limiting the rule to uneven gaps. With even gaps she has a וסת, and under רבי דוסא she stays with דיה שעתה. This fully answers the problem raised in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say: introduces a second answer

phrases.english: And if you want, say this is what it means:
not when she was even,
but only when she decreased or increased,
but if she was even, she has set up a fixed cycle,
and her time is enough.
And whose view is this? It is רבי דוסא.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read the ברייתא. Under the רבנן, she is retroactively impure even with even intervals. Under רבי דוסא, even intervals set up a וסת, so דיה שעתה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same challenge, offered in place of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the wording differently and naming whose view it is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Even" seemed to include the even case as the obvious one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא leaves out the even case: even sightings make a וסת and דיה שעתה, following רבי דוסא.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's line in the משנה: any woman who went three עונות without seeing blood is in the דיה שעתה category.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: any woman who has gone three cycles without seeing, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting רבי אליעזר's words from the משנה. It is setting up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר widens the דיה שעתה leniency. It is not only for certain women. It covers any woman who stopped seeing for three עונות. The "וכו׳" means the rest of the line in the משנה should be filled in.

keyTerms.meaning: passed over her: she went through that time without seeing blood
etc.: the rest of the משנה's line is assumed
any woman: not limited to special cases

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says:
Any woman who has gone, etc.
phrases.notes: Fill in from the משנה: who has gone three cycles without seeing blood, her time is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: כָּל אִשָּׁה שֶׁעָבְרוּ עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the זקנה ברייתא and goes back to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any woman who has gone three עונות without seeing blood is impure only from the time she sees (דיה שעתה).

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's proof: the girl from הַיְתָלוֹ
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר tells the חכמים about a real case: a girl in הַיְתָלוֹ stopped seeing for three עונות, and the חכמים ruled דיה שעתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר said to the חכמים: There was a case of a girl in הַיְתָלוֹ who stopped seeing for three cycles. The case came before the חכמים, and they said: her time is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר proves his view from an actual ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The girl was not pregnant, nursing, or old. She simply stopped for three עונות. Since the חכמים still ruled דיה שעתה, רבי אליעזר argues that the leniency applies to any woman, just as he said in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: a real case that happened, used as proof
she stopped: did not see blood

steps.whyThisMatters: A ruling given in a real case is strong support. It shows the leniency does not depend on age, pregnancy, or nursing.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לַחֲכָמִים:
phrases.english: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר said to the חכמים:
There was a case with a certain girl in הַיְתָלוֹ,
who stopped seeing for three cycles,
and the case came before the חכמים,
and they said: her time is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לַחֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבי אליעזר's line in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's rule that any woman who stopped for three עונות has דיה שעתה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the חכמים' ruling about a girl in הַיְתָלוֹ.

steps.title: The Sages reject the real case as proof
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי אליעזר that a ruling made under pressure is no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: a ruling made in a time of pressure is no proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on the story רבי אליעזר just told about the girl in הַיְתָלוֹ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They do not deny that the story happened. They say the lenient ruling was given because of special pressure, so it cannot teach the normal הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: a time of pressure or emergency

phrases.english: They said to him:
A time of pressure is no proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין שְׁעַת הַדְּחָק רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the הַיְתָלוֹ case as proof for the regular halacha.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling was made under special pressure, so it was not a normal ruling.

steps.title: What was the pressure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the שעת הדחק was in that story.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the time of pressure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question, and this sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said there was pressure, but the story never said what it was. The גמרא wants to know what pushed them to be lenient.

phrases.english: What was the time of pressure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details behind the claim in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What emergency led to the lenient ruling in הַיְתָלוֹ.

steps.title: First answer: years of famine
steps.stepSummary: Some say those were years of famine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: they were years of famine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first explanation of the pressure: it was a time of famine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a famine, declaring food impure would waste scarce food. So the חכמים ruled leniently to avoid making things worse.

phrases.english: Some say: they were years of famine,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.

steps.title: Second answer: many pure items were at stake
steps.stepSummary: Others say the girl had handled many pure items, and the חכמים worried about losing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: she had handled many pure items, and the חכמים were concerned about losing those pure items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation of the pressure: a lot of טהרות would be lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she were impure מעת לעת, everything pure she touched in the past day would become impure. The חכמים ruled דיה שעתה to save those items, so this was a special case.

phrases.english: Some say: she had handled many pure items,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the word in square brackets. Both mean she worked with pure items.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis were concerned about the loss of the pure items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to Step 19, instead of the famine answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pressure was the large loss of טהרות.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both answers agree on the main point: the lenient ruling came from outside pressure, not from the regular הלכה.

steps.title: רבי ruled like רבי אליעזר under pressure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that רבי once followed רבי אליעזר, and after he remembered, said רבי אליעזר can be relied on in a time of pressure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: there was a case, and רבי ruled like רבי אליעזר. After he remembered, he said: רבי אליעזר is worthy to rely on in a time of pressure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about רבי ruling in practice like רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that רבי אליעזר's view, even though others argue, can be used in an emergency. The phrase 'after he remembered' is unclear, and the גמרא will ask about it next.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: there was a case,
and רבי acted like רבי אליעזר.
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: After he remembered, he said:
רבי אליעזר is worthy
to rely on in a time of pressure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה, וְעָשָׂה רַבִּי כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects to the idea of שעת הדחק from Step 18 and shows רבי using it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's lenient view may be relied on in a time of pressure.

steps.title: What does 'after he remembered' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי remembered.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'after he remembered' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the unclear words in the ברייתא, and this sets up its first suggested answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not say what רבי remembered. How we read it decides how strong רבי אליעזר's view is.

phrases.english: What does "after he remembered" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the ברייתא of Step 22.

steps.title: If the halacha was decided against him, how could רבי follow him?
steps.stepSummary: Suppose he remembered that the הלכה follows the רבנן. Then how could he follow רבי אליעזר even under pressure?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he remembered that the הלכה is not like רבי אליעזר but like the רבנן, then how could he act like him even in a time of pressure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one reading of 'after he remembered' and shows it cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a final הלכה was set against רבי אליעזר, his view is simply rejected. A rejected view cannot be used even in an emergency, so this reading fails.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
how could he act like him?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying the הלכה follows the רבנן. It is testing that idea and showing it cannot fit the ברייתא.

phrases.english: If you say: after he remembered
that the halacha is not like רבי אליעזר
but like the Rabbis,
then in a time of pressure, how could he act like him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא לְאַחַר שֶׁנִּזְכַּר דְּאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a possible answer to Step 23 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי remembered a final ruling against רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A view that was officially rejected cannot be followed even in an emergency, yet רבי did follow it.

steps.title: No final ruling, but many sages disagreed
steps.stepSummary: No הלכה had been decided either way. רבי remembered that many sages, not just one, argued with רבי אליעזר, so he allowed relying on him only in a time of pressure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, no הלכה was said either like this sage or like that sage. What does 'after he remembered' mean? After he remembered that not one sage but many disagreed with him, he said: רבי אליעזר is worthy to rely on in a time of pressure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading of 'after he remembered.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no final ruling was made, רבי אליעזר's view is not rejected. But a view opposed by many is weak in normal times, so it may be used only under pressure.

keyTerms.meaning: neither like this sage nor like that sage

steps.whatToRemember: An opinion against the majority, when no final הלכה was decided, may be relied on in a time of pressure (שעת הדחק).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the idea that a minority view can be used בשעת הדחק when the הלכה was never finally decided against it.

phrases.english: Rather, the halacha was not stated
neither like this sage nor like that sage,
And what does "after he remembered" mean?

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר שֶׁנִּזְכַּר דְּלָאו יָחִיד פְּלִיג עֲלֵיהּ,
phrases.english: After he remembered that it was not one sage who disagreed with him,
but many disagreed with him,
he said: רבי אליעזר is worthy
to rely on in a time of pressure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּלָא אִיתְּמַר הִילְכְתָא לָא כְּמָר וָלֹא כְּמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of Step 24 with a reading that works.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'After he remembered' meant he remembered a final ruling against רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: No final ruling existed. He remembered that many sages disagreed, which makes the view usable only under pressure.

steps.title: A young girl who sees blood before her time
steps.stepSummary: A girl too young to see blood who saw: the first and second times get דיה שעתה. After the third time she is like all women and is impure מעת לעת and מפקידה לפקידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a young girl whose time to see blood has not come, and she saw: the first time, her time is enough; the second time, her time is enough; the third time, she is like all women and makes things impure for the past 24 hours and back to her last check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a young girl who saw blood before the normal age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like a girl who never saw before, she is lenient (דיה שעתה) at first because she has no pattern of seeing. After three sightings she counts as a regular woman, so the normal backward impurity applies.

keyTerms.meaning: a young girl who has not yet reached the age of seeing blood
from one check to the previous check
like all women, the regular rule

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: a young girl
whose time to see blood has not come, and she saw:
the first time, her time is enough;
the second time, her time is enough;
the third time, she is like all women,
and she makes things impure for the past 24 hours
and back to her last check.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: תִּינוֹקֶת שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּהּ לִרְאוֹת וְרָאֲתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on another woman who gets דיה שעתה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A young girl gets דיה שעתה for her first two sightings. After the third she is like all women: impure מעת לעת and מפקידה לפקידה.

steps.title: Breaks of three cycles bring back the leniency
steps.stepSummary: After the young girl became like all women, a gap of three עונות followed by seeing gives her דיה שעתה again. This happens twice. After the third such gap she is like all women.
steps.simpleTranslation: If three cycles passed and she saw, her time is enough. If three more cycles passed and she saw, her time is enough. If three more cycles passed and she saw, she is like all women and is impure for the past twenty-four hours or back to her last check.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the case of the young girl from Step 26. Now it adds what happens when she goes three עונות without seeing and then sees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A break of three עונות resets her, so she gets the easy rule of דיה שעתה again. She gets it after the first break and after the second break. After the third break the long gaps have become her regular pattern, so she is treated like any adult woman and gets the stricter rule of מעת לעת and מפקידה לפקידה.

keyTerms.meaning: One expected cycle, about thirty days
Her time is enough: she is impure only from the moment she saw, not backward
From time to time: impurity reaches back a full twenty-four hours
From check to check: impurity reaches back to her last clean check (if that is shorter than twenty-four hours)
Like all women: she loses the special leniency and follows the normal rule

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two counts. In Step 26 she counted three sightings. Here she counts three breaks of three עונות each, and each break comes before a new sighting.

phrases.english: If three cycles passed over her and then she saw,
phrases.notes: This is the same young girl who just became 'like all women' at the end of Step 26.

phrases.english: her time is enough;

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד עָבְרוּ עָלֶיהָ שָׁלֹשׁ עוֹנוֹת וְרָאֲתָה —
phrases.english: and if again three cycles passed over her and she saw,
her time is enough;

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד עָבְרוּ עָלֶיהָ שָׁלֹשׁ עוֹנוֹת וְרָאֲתָה —
phrases.english: and if again three cycles passed over her and she saw,
she is like all women,
and she makes things impure for twenty-four hours back
and from check to check.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from Step 26 and adds the case of breaks of three עונות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the first two breaks of three עונות brings back דיה שעתה. After the third break she is like all women, impure מעת לעת and מפקידה לפקידה.

steps.title: A girl old enough to see blood
steps.stepSummary: A girl who has reached the age of seeing gets דיה שעתה only the first time. The second time she is impure מעת לעת and מפקידה לפקידה. After a break of three עונות, she gets דיה שעתה again.
steps.simpleTranslation: When she reached the age to see: the first time, her time is enough. The second time, she is impure for twenty-four hours back or back to her last check. If three cycles passed and she saw, her time is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a second kind of girl: one who has reached the age when seeing blood is expected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The younger girl got the leniency for two sightings. This girl gets it for only one, because at her age seeing is normal, so she becomes like all women more quickly. But a break of three עונות still brings back דיה שעתה, as רבי אליעזר holds for any woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Her time to see has arrived: she has reached the age when seeing blood is expected

steps.whatToRemember: The younger girl gets דיה שעתה for two sightings, but the girl who has reached the age of seeing gets it for only one. For both of them, a break of three עונות brings back דיה שעתה.

phrases.english: And when her time to see has arrived:
the first time, her time is enough;
the second time, she makes things impure for twenty-four hours back
and from check to check;
if three cycles passed over her and she saw,
her time is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with a second, older girl and compares her to the younger girl.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl who reached the age of seeing gets דיה שעתה only the first time. From the second time she is impure מעת לעת and מפקידה לפקידה, and a break of three עונות brings back דיה שעתה.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes a line of the ברייתא to discuss it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the line 'three cycles passed over her, her time is enough' in order to examine it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If three cycles passed over her, her time is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes one line from the ברייתא so it can ask about it or explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is ruled here. The line is pulled out because the גמרא wants to look closely at why a break of three עונות gives a girl who already became like all women the leniency of דיה שעתה again.

keyTerms.meaning: Passed over her: time went by without her seeing blood

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This is the usual way the גמרא quotes a line from the teaching it just brought, here the ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: עָבְרוּ עָלֶיהָ שָׁלֹשׁ עוֹנוֹת — דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ.
phrases.english: If three cycles passed over her, her time is enough.
phrases.notes: This is the last line of the ברייתא in Step 28, about the girl who has already reached the age of seeing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the whole ברייתא has been quoted, the גמרא goes back to one line of it to begin analyzing it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the ruling that after three עונות without seeing, the girl gets דיה שעתה, as the starting point for a discussion.
